This lecture examines how depthwise separable convolutions enable real-time computer vision on mobile and edge devices. Standard convolution performs spatial filtering and cross-channel feature combination simultaneously in a single heavy operation.
A depthwise convolution applies a single spatial filter independently to each input channel. A pointwise 1 by 1 convolution projects and combines the channel outputs linearly.

Recognizing both tiny distant objects and large foreground objects requires combining high-resolution spatial detail from early layers with rich semantic context from deep layers. To train pixelwise segmentation models underclass imbalance between foreground objects and background sky or road pixels, engineers combined cross-entropy.
